design_rule: Every cross-word or cross-passage connection must declare an explicit relation type from {cognate, word_formation, borrowing, translation, interpretation, comparison}. 'cognate' edges are restricted to items sharing an established language family; cross-family links must use translation, borrowing, interpretation, or comparison.

nodes.gloss: on foot, pedestrian (true Slavic reflex of *ped-; contrast нога from *noga)
foot, leg (from Proto-Slavic *noga 'claw/hoof', NOT from *ped-; corrects HS-T005 Turn 3)
foot, leg; to be sufficient (Kojiki / modern kanji usage)
peace (primary Septuagint rendering of shalom, not a cognate)
deliverance, safety, salvation (contextual Septuagint rendering of shalom)
compact, peace (Vulgate rendering of eirene/shalom; PIE *pak- 'fasten')
way, path; to speak/guide (Dao De Jing 1; modern Chinese versions of John 1:1 also render logos as 道)
root, trunk base, origin (indicative stroke at base of 木)
forest, shrine woods (graphic + on'yomi borrowing paired with native kun'yomi mori)

clusters.title: Foot and Stepping (PIE Cognates vs Cross-Family Non-Cognates)
clusters.summary: Contrasts genuine Indo-European sound-change reflexes of *ped- against unrelated words in five other families, and corrects the archive's earlier Russian noga error.

clusters.title: Peace and Wholeness (Semitic Cognates vs Septuagint/Vulgate Translation)
clusters.summary: Separates inherited Semitic cognates (Hebrew shalom / Arabic salam) from textual translation choices into Greek (eirene, soteria) and Latin (pax).

clusters.title: Word, Account, and Way (Biblical and Classical Translation Chain)
clusters.summary: Traces Psalm 33:6 and John 1:1 across Hebrew dabar, Greek logos, Latin verbum, and Chinese dao without collapsing them into a fake shared root.

clusters.title: Writing, Letterform, and Book
clusters.summary: Compares Semitic trilateral root pattern (*k-t-b -> katav/ktav, kataba/kitab) with Greek grapho/gramma, Latin scribo, and Chinese brush-based shu.

clusters.title: Tree, Root, and Compositional Radicals
clusters.summary: Demonstrates morphographic character composition from radical 木 (tree) into 本 (root), 林 (grove), and 森 (forest) and Sinospheric graphic borrowing into Japanese.

edges.evidence: Inherited Indo-Iranian reflex preserving initial *p- and dental stop.
Inherited Hellenic o-grade nominative pous, oblique stem pod-.
Inherited Italic e-grade nominative pes, oblique stem ped-.
Germanic lengthened o-grade with Grimm's Law (*p > f, *d > t).
Inherited Balto-Slavic derivative (*ped-sjo- > peshij 'on foot').
Lexical replacement within Slavic: noga descends from *noga ('claw/unguis'), not *ped-.
Orthographic adoption of Han character 足 to write native Japanese word ashi / tariru.
Unrelated Sino-Tibetan morphograph pairing 'foot' with 'sufficiency'.
Unrelated Uralic lexeme covering both foot and leg.
Unrelated Bantu noun-class 3/4 lexeme.
Unrelated Turkic lexeme (*hadak > ayak).
Unrelated Uto-Aztecan noun with absolutive suffix -tl.
Northwest Semitic reflex (*š > sh, Canaanite shift *ā > ō).
Central Semitic reflex (*š > s, preserved long ā).
Standard Greek translation choice for Hebrew shalom; unrelated Indo-European etymology.
Shows translation is passage-sensitive rather than a mechanical 1-to-1 lexical substitution.
Jerome renders eirene/shalom with Latin pax ('compact/treaty peace').
Septuagint renders Hebrew dabar ('word/speech/matter') with Greek logos.
Vulgate narrows polysemous Greek logos ('speech/account/reason') into Latin verbum ('word').
Chinese biblical translators chose 道 (dao) to carry the cosmic/ordering register of Johannine logos alongside its Classical sense 'to speak'.
Inherited Semitic trilateral root *k-t-b in Qal stem.
Nominal vowel-pattern derivation from כ-ת-ב meaning 'script/handwriting'.
Inherited Semitic Form I verb kataba.
Fi'al nominal template on root ك-ت-ب yielding kitab ('book/writing').
Resultative -ma noun from grapho ('that which is drawn/written').
Parallel semantic shift ('scratch/incise' -> 'write') on distinct PIE roots (*gerbh- vs *skreybh-).
Contrasts consonantal template derivation with brush-depicting morphograph 書.
Indicative (zhishi) stroke added to base of 木 to denote 'root/origin'.
Compound ideograph (huiyi) pairing two 木 graphs for 'grove/woods'.
Triplicated 木 graph intensifying density to 'deep forest'.
Chinese character 森 adopted into Japanese for both Sino-Japanese reading shin and native mori.

passages.text: בְּרֵאשִׁית בָּרָא אֱלֹהִים אֵת הַשָּׁמַיִם וְאֵת הָאָרֶץ

passages.text: 道可道非常道名可名非常名
passages.transliteration: Dao ke dao fei chang dao; ming ke ming fei chang ming
passages.gloss: The Way that can be spoken is not the constant Way; the name that can be named is not the constant name
passages.practice_note: Tianzige square-grid character balance: observe 道 functioning sequentially as noun ('Way') and verb ('to speak').
